# 2 Baruch Chapter 50 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Fourth Fast and Dialogue
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 50:1 — opening divine response formula

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Hear, O-Baruch, this-word, and-write in-the-remembrance-of-your-heart" |
| LOGOS | "Hear, O Baruch, this word, and write in the memory of your heart" |
| PNEUMA | "Listen, Baruch — write all of this in the memory of your heart" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. 'Remembrance' (EMET) and 'memory' (LOGOS/PNEUMA) both translate the Syriac dukhrana; 'memory of your heart' is the more idiomatic Syriac phrase and LOGOS preserves it fully.

---

## 50:2 — earth as custodian of the dead

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "it-receives-them now in-order-to-keep-them, not-changing-anything in-their-form" |
| LOGOS | "it receives them now in order to keep them, not changing anything in their form" |
| PNEUMA | "It receives them now to hold them, making no changes to their form" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. The formal structure 'in order to keep them' reflects the Syriac purposive clause better than PNEUMA's condensed 'to hold them'.
